description: The first cluster, shown in red, deals with topics such as triple helix (e.g. Ref. [124], networking (e.g. Ref. [125], and national innovation systems. Given the increasing dispersal of innovation actors and the fact that innovation requires collecting various resources, rarely all of which are available to one actor, the creation of innovation networks composed of representatives of different stakeholders is necessary to exchange information and resources for innovation [12]. Also, as innovation has become a collective game, the participation of actors from government, firms, and universities is required for innovation.

The second cluster, shown in green, includes studies on sustainable transition (e.g. Ref. [14], socio-technical systems (e.g. Ref. [26], and sustainability. These issues, given the importance of environmental concerns, the optimal use of resources, and the need for efficient technologies, are expected to be addressed in research, so that with increasing awareness of environmental degradation, the need for optimal energy consumption, and the need to move towards eco-efficient economies, it is necessary to adopt new approaches to sustainable transition analysis [10,14]. In addition, most systematic approaches mainly focus on the production side and pay little attention to the user side. The socio-technical systems approach is more appropriate for analysis as it involves both parties [26].

The third cluster, shown in blue, deals with knowledge sharing (e.g., Ref. [132] and regional studies (e.g., Ref. [90]. Given the knowledge-driven economies and globalization of knowledge production, it is expected that the knowledge base associated with innovation will no longer be limited to specific national or regional boundaries and that knowledge will be scattered around the world [99]. Therefore, the need to optimally combine these scattered knowledge sets and implement innovations should be taken into account.

The fourth cluster, shown in yellow, deals with the review (e.g. Ref. [134], comparative (e.g. Ref. [121], and methodological (e.g., Ref. [23] studies. Due to the expansion of research in the field of innovation systems and the increasing dispersion of content in this field, it is necessary to conduct research to integrate and combine these issues.
